questions.knowledge_point: Writing the Lower Riemann Sum for a Function That's Neither Strictly Increasing Nor Decreasing
questions.problem:
Let $R=[1,4]\times [1,2]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=4x-2y.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}={{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}},\,{P}_{2}={{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the lower Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
L(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
questions.worked_solution:
The lower Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{m}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${m}_{ij}$ is the *minimum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093975/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=4x-2y$ increases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=4x-2y$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093975/assets/01b291ca7cd81b88cf6ed06fdcdb2ffcbb1f78255d0f57d496823d347c2fb0b3.png)

As a result, the *minimum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *largest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *top left corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093975/assets/a44c2586978022663635d1f35399166c1ae32963fe0f4bffebd21966ad40bac5.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i-1},{y}_{j})=4{x}_{i-1}-2{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the lower Riemann sum is

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}_{(}f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(4{x}_{i-1}-2{y}_{j})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $4{x}_{i-1}-2{y}_{j}.$
